claim_set.claim_text: Every AI-assisted AML action that moves toward a consequential action MUST map to a recorded named-authority decision — the agent, the AML artefact (alert, screening hit, SAR/STR draft, onboarding case), the intended consequential action, and the named compliance officer / MLRO / BSA officer under whose authority it proceeds. Actions lacking a recorded authority decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate.

Before an AI-assisted AML action proceeds to a consequential action it MUST carry a recorded due-diligence result — a CDD / KYC determination (FATF R.10; FinCEN CDD Rule), a screening determination (sanctions / PEP / adverse-media match assessment), and a risk determination (FATF R.1) where applicable. An unscreened, low-confidence, or due-diligence-deficient action is refused.

Every AI-assisted AML action that proceeds toward a consequential action MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable provenance pin binding the generating model and version, the screened lists and list versions / pinned source data, the due-diligence result relied on, and the named-authority outcome — audit-grade, examiner-verifiable provenance verifiable offline, satisfying FATF R.11 and FinCEN / BSA record-keeping (31 CFR Chapter X).

An AI-assisted AML action MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT drive a consequential action until a named human reviewer — the compliance officer, the MLRO / nominated officer, or the BSA officer — records sign-off. The SAR/STR filing additionally requires §36 two-person sign-off (the drafting analyst AND an approving MLRO / BSA officer). Unreviewed AI-driven consequential actions are refused and routed dual-channel.

KYE governs WHETHER an AI-assisted AML action may proceed at the action boundary and PROVES the basis. KYE does not run transaction-monitoring models, does not decide whether a transaction is truly money-laundering, and does not replace the institution's AML program.
